title: Questions to Ask During an Initial Architect Consultation in Scarsdale
excerpt: An initial consultation with a residential architect in Scarsdale should cover your vision, budget, timeline, and the permitting process. Here are the questions that matter most.
content:
You've decided to remodel your kitchen, add a second story, or tackle a major renovation to your Scarsdale home. Now you're looking for the right architect and general contractor to make it happen. The initial consultation is your chance to ask real questions and get a clear sense of how the project will work.

This conversation matters. It sets the tone for everything that follows. The right questions will help you understand what to expect, how decisions get made, and whether the architect and contractor you're talking to can actually deliver what you're imagining.

Ask About Their Experience and How They Work

Start by asking what kinds of projects the architect has completed in Scarsdale and throughout Westchester. A licensed architect based in Westchester, NY who has worked in your town understands the local style, the neighborhood character, and how to work with the building department there.

Ask whether they personally oversee every project or whether work gets handed off to other team members. There's a real difference between a principal architect who touches everything and a firm where your project might move around. Ask who you'll actually be talking to throughout the process.

If you're looking at a design-build approach, ask how the architect and contractor coordinate. With a design-build firm, the same team handles both the planning and the construction, which can reduce confusion and finger-pointing if something needs to change mid-project.

Understand the Process and the Permit Timeline

Every municipality in Westchester County, including Scarsdale, has its own building department and permit requirements. Ask the architect what permits your specific project will need and roughly how long the approval process typically takes in Scarsdale.

This is important because it affects your timeline. A general contractor in Westchester who knows the local review process can give you realistic expectations. Don't let anyone tell you that Scarsdale's permitting is unusually slow or fast compared to nearby towns. Every town has its process, and a good architect knows how to work within it.

Ask what documents you'll need to prepare before submitting to the Scarsdale building department. Ask whether the architect will handle the permit application or whether that's your responsibility.

Talk About Budget, Timeline, and Decisions

Be direct about your budget range. You don't need to share an exact number, but the architect needs to know the ballpark so they can design a home renovation in Westchester NY that makes sense for you. Ask how changes to the design will be handled if costs start trending in the wrong direction.

Ask about the construction timeline. When can work start? How long will the project typically take? What might cause delays?

Ask how design decisions happen. Will you review drawings before they go to the permit stage? How many rounds of revisions are included? Who has the final say on materials and finishes?

A good residential architect in Scarsdale will answer these questions directly. They'll explain their process clearly and help you feel confident about moving forward.
